consumed.resolution: merged into blocker-proof-accepts-a-protected-acs-predicate (backlog review D5, PR #1571): same goal and shared files; its acceptance, files and deps now live on blocker-proof-accepts-a-protected-acs-predicate

fix: Design first (design review before build). Candidate: a failure explains through a proven protected test file when the failing test names a test function that is declared in that file (resolve the name against the worktree source), and a plain unit-test failure becomes explainable only in that case. Reject any rule that excuses a failure by package alone.
summary: Cycle 2508: the floor failures were './cmd/evolve: unit tests FAIL' (--- FAIL: TestParallelDefault_EveryTopLevelTestIsParallelOrListedSerial) and an integration-tag failure of the same test. buildFloorExplainable (go/internal/core/build_blocker_exit.go:28) accepts only cover-strict and ./acs/cycleN predicate failures, and explainedFailure (go/internal/core/blocker_proof.go) needs the failure text to name the proven file. The guard failure names neither the kind nor the file (the guard reports the test name TestWireOrchestratorDeps_RequestChannelWired, which lives in the protected go/cmd/evolve/request_channel_test.go). So after blocker-proof-refuses-a-protected-test-file lands, a 2508-shaped cycle gets a proven claim plus 'these failures are not explained' and still runs repair rounds.
title: a proven blocker cannot explain a guard test failure that names no file, so the cycle still runs repair rounds
